transcript.text: Six school days later at 16:35, Speaker B and Speaker A are alone in the music room before the club meeting. The instruments are closed, Person this conversation is absent and has sent no shared message, the hallway is open, and late light falls across the room.

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text: “About the message,” Setsuna said. “You said it could wait. Has it waited long enough?”

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text:
Kazusa rested her palm on the closed piano lid.

“No.”

She looked toward the open hallway.

“It can wait until after the meeting.”

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text: “After the meeting,” Setsuna repeated. “All right. I’ll remember.”

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text:
Kazusa lifted her hand from the piano lid.

“Don’t turn it into a promise.”

She moved to the nearest chair and sat down.

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text:
“I’m not asking for one,” Setsuna said. “I just heard you.”

She turned toward the closed instruments. “What are we playing today?”

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text:
Kazusa glanced at the closed piano.

“Your choice.”

She stood and opened the fallboard.

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text:
“Then something quiet,” Setsuna said. “I’ll take the first verse.”

She drew a breath and waited for the piano.

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text:
Kazusa let the silence sit for one beat, then lowered her fingers to the keys.

The opening was soft, spare, and steady.

transcript.label: Scene 1
transcript.text: At 17:20 on Friday, Person C has just left the laboratory for the costume fitting she mentioned to both of them earlier. Speaker this conversation and Speaker A remain alone. The usual Friday bakery bag holds one unlabeled bun on a napkin between two paper cups; it is untouched. The laboratory door is open, no other errand is pending, and neither person is required to stay.

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text:
Okabe studies the untouched bun, then raises one finger as though announcing a classified experiment.

“Friday’s unidentified bakery specimen has entered the dangerous phase. Kurisu, can you identify it from the evidence, or must I demonstrate the superior method of random selection?”

His hand hovers above the napkin.

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text: Kurisu lays two fingers over the edge of the napkin, leaving the bun untouched, and fixes his raised finger with a flat look. “Random selection is not a method; it’s surrender with extra steps. Make your guess first.”

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text:
Okabe’s raised finger curls toward his chin. He leans over the napkin, inspecting the bun without touching it.

“Then my first hypothesis is sweet red-bean paste,” he says with solemnity disproportionate to the evidence. “A classic concealment. If I am wrong, the failure belongs to the bakery’s counterintelligence.”

He taps the table once beside the napkin and waits.

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text: Kurisu takes the bun, bites off a careful piece, and chews before setting the remainder back on the napkin. “Pear-custard. The bakery’s counterintelligence is apparently just poor labeling.”

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text:
Okabe’s mouth tightens as he looks from the remaining bun to Kurisu. He lifts the piece, takes a small bite, and chews with exaggerated severity.

“Pear-custard…” He points at the napkin. “An acceptable result. But the labeling failure remains a hostile act against scientific inquiry.”

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text: Kurisu keeps her fingers off the remaining bite and gives him a flat look. “A missing label is not a hostile act. It’s a missing label. Record the error before you indict the pastry.”

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text:
Okabe holds the remaining bite above the napkin, then lowers it without taking another bite. With his free hand, he makes a solemn mark in the air.

“Error recorded: pear-custard, label absent, indictment contested.” He nods once. “The tribunal will reconvene when the bakery commits a second offense.”

He leaves the bite on the napkin and looks at Kurisu.

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text: Kurisu draws her cup closer, leaving the last bite on the napkin. “Then adjourn the tribunal. One missing label is an error, not a pattern.”
The previous meeting ended; time has passed before this return.
Several ordinary school and laboratory days pass. Neither person receives a further shared explanation of the bun after Person C leaves for the fitting.

transcript.label: Scene 2
transcript.text: Four school days later at 18:10, Speaker this conversation and Speaker A stand below the laboratory stairs. The station is direct from the corner; the longer route begins across the street through the arcade. On earlier walks, Speaker this conversation has given theatrical reasons to take the arcade, Speaker A has corrected them, and Person C has stopped at the window there. Person C is absent for a commitment both of them know about. No route has been proposed, the stairwell door is open, and either person can leave.

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text:
Okabe steps through the stairwell door and points across the street toward the arcade.

“The direct route is a trap laid by convenience itself,” he declares. “We take the arcade. A proper investigator does not ignore a controlled detour.”

He keeps his arm extended toward the longer route.

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text: Kurisu steps toward the arcade and pauses at the curb. “Fine—the arcade. It’s a longer route, not a controlled detour. What question are you pretending to investigate?”

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text:
Okabe lowers his hand, eyes fixed on the arcade window.

“Whether a familiar route remains the same when the person who stops at that window is absent,” he says. “A modest question, perhaps—but not one to be dismissed without fieldwork.”

He steps to the curb and waits.

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text: Kurisu comes to the curb, eyes on the arcade window. “The route is the same. The stop isn’t. Those are different variables.” She steps into the crossing toward the arcade.

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text:
Okabe pauses for half a beat at the curb, then follows into the crossing, keeping his gaze on the arcade window.

“Exactly. Different variables.” He lifts his chin. “Then the route is our control, and the missing stop is the result. The Future Gadget Laboratory will observe.”

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text: Kurisu keeps walking toward the arcade, her gaze fixed ahead. “The route is the control; the missing stop is a condition, not a result. Don’t turn an absence into data.”

transcript.speaker: Speaker B
transcript.text:
Okabe’s raised hand drops. He walks three steps in silence, then glances toward the arcade window.

“Then it is only an absence,” he says. “Unmeasured. Unresolved.”

He keeps walking.

transcript.speaker: Speaker A
transcript.text: Kurisu passes the window without stopping. “Unmeasured and unresolved, perhaps. But not ‘only.’ That word is doing too much work.”
